0.title: cattery

1.text:
A room is a module that enables other modules with lib.mkDefault. It does not add configuration of its own. Enabling a room also enables the rooms it depends on. This is the NixOS graph: room.basis
 ├─ room.general                 (basis + boot.efi)
 ├─ room.server-mini             (basis + acme, optional cloud-init and qemu-guest)
 │   └─ room.server              (server-mini)
 │       └─ room.server.nas      (server + optional storage services)
 ├─ room.container               (basis + acme, boot.isContainer)
 └─ room.desktop.basis           (basis + desktop hardware and fonts)
     └─ room.desktop.general     (desktop.basis + boot.efi)
         ├─ room.desktop.dev      (desktop.general + dev tools)
         ├─ room.desktop.game     (desktop.general + steam)
         └─ room.desktop.wsl      (desktop.basis + wsl) Home-manager has its own smaller chain and a standalone room.game. nix-darwin provides room.basis and room.desktop.dev. Because sub-module enables use lib.mkDefault, explicit settings take precedence: cattery.room.desktop.dev.enable = true;
cattery.apps.jetbrains.enable = false; # use neovim instead
1.title: What is a room?

68.text:
A room is a module that enables other modules with lib.mkDefault. Enabling one room enables its dependencies, so a single option can turn on a set of related features. All sub-module enables use lib.mkDefault, so explicit settings take precedence. The NixOS room graph: room.basis
 ├─ room.general                 (basis + boot.efi)
 ├─ room.server-mini             (basis + acme, optional cloud-init and qemu-guest)
 │   └─ room.server              (server-mini)
 │       └─ room.server.nas      (server + optional storage services)
 ├─ room.container               (basis + acme, boot.isContainer)
 └─ room.desktop.basis           (basis + desktop hardware and fonts)
     └─ room.desktop.general     (desktop.basis + boot.efi)
         ├─ room.desktop.dev      (desktop.general + dev tools)
         ├─ room.desktop.game     (desktop.general + steam)
         └─ room.desktop.wsl      (desktop.basis + wsl) Home-manager has a separate chain and a standalone room.game. nix-darwin provides room.basis and room.desktop.dev.
68.title: Rooms

69.text:
Rooms exist in the NixOS, home-manager, and nix-darwin module sets. The NixOS set has the largest graph. The home-manager set has its own chain, and the darwin set has only two rooms. Enabling desktop.dev in the NixOS set enables desktop.general, then desktop.basis, then basis. To override a room, set the individual module option. The room default loses because lib.mkDefault has a lower priority than a normal assignment: cattery.room.desktop.dev.enable = true;
cattery.apps.jetbrains.enable = false;
69.title: How rooms work

101.title: Module conventions

102.text: Namespace: Use ${namespace}. The flake sets it to cattery.Enable option: Most modules have an enable option.extraOptions: Many modules expose extraOptions = mkOption { type = attrs; default = { }; } and merge it into the underlying options.persistence: Many home-manager modules that write state have a persistence option, default true.Platform checks: Use purr.meta.isLinux and purr.meta.isDarwin for platform-specific code.Rooms: Use mkDefaultEnabled from lib.cattery.module for sub-module enables.
102.title: Key conventions

103.text: PrefixPurposefeat/New features or modulesfix/Bug fixeschore/Maintenance and dependency updatesdocs/Documentation
103.title: Branch naming

104.text:
Create a branch from main.Make changes.Test locally:nix flake check     # lint and evaluate all 262 modules
nix fmt             # format all filesOptionally test on a real machine:nixos-rebuild test --flake .#myhost
home-manager switch --flake .#alicePush the branch and open a pull request against main.Get at least one review approval.On merge to main, FlakeHub publishes a new rolling release.
104.title: Workflow

105.text: Pull requests to main run nix flake check. The check includes: nixfmt: format checkdeadnix: dead code checkstatix: lint checkmodule-eval: import and call check for all 262 module files A push to main triggers the FlakeHub workflow, which publishes a rolling release at nixcafe/cattery-modules.
105.title: CI

106.text: Create the module file in the appropriate directory:NixOS: modules/nixos/<category>/<name>/default.nixShared between module sets: modules/shared/<category>/<name>/default.nixCross-platform home-manager: modules/home/shared/<category>/<name>/default.nixNixOS-specific home-manager: modules/home/nixos/<category>/<name>/default.nixDarwin-specific home-manager: modules/home/darwin/<category>/<name>/default.nixAdd enable and any module-specific options. Add extraOptions when the module wraps a NixOS or home-manager option set.If the module needs secrets, add a companion secrets/default.nix and use mkAppSecretsOption or mkHomeAppSecretsOption from lib.cattery.secrets.Add the module to a room when appropriate. Use mkDefaultEnabled for sub-module enables.Run nix flake check and nix fmt.
106.title: Adding a module

107.text: Pull request reviews are required (at least one approval).Status checks must pass before merging.Stale reviews are dismissed when new commits are pushed.
107.title: Branch protection

108.text: cattery integrates agenix for encrypted secrets. Service modules that need configuration files have a companion secrets module. The companion module adds the encrypted files to age.secrets. Many of these modules also link the decrypted file into /etc.
108.title: Secrets & agenix

109.text:
cattery.secrets.secretsPath defaults to <user.home>/agenix. The files under that directory are grouped by scope: <secretsPath>/
├── hosts/<host>/global/        # host-specific, root-owned
├── hosts/<host>/users/<user>/  # host-specific, user-owned
├── shared/global/              # shared across hosts, root-owned
└── shared/users/<user>/        # shared across hosts, user-owned If you keep secrets in your flake, point the option at that directory: cattery.secrets.secretsPath = ./secrets; The keys in secrets.nix must match the file paths under secretsPath.

115.text: cattery.secrets.yubikey.enable is declared, but the current module does not add age-plugin-yubikey. The package override is commented out in modules/shared/secrets/default.nix, so enabling the option alone does not configure a YubiKey identity. To use a YubiKey, add the plugin and the identity path through the agenix options.
